rulebook: HHSC Minimum Standards for Child-Care Centers (26 TAC Ch. 746), revised December 2025

items.requirement: Parents may visit the center during hours of operation without prior approval to observe their child and program.
items.quote: Ensuring parents can visit the child-care center any time during the child-care center's hours of operation to observe their child, program activities, the building, the grounds, and the equipment without having to secure prior approval

items.requirement: If the center does not carry required liability insurance, parents must be notified in writing before admission.
items.quote: If you do not carry liability insurance that meets the requirements of §746.203 of this division (relating to What are the liability insurance requirements?), then you must notify the parent of each child in your care in writing that you do not carry liability insurance before you admit the child into your care.

items.requirement: The center must have written operational policies and procedures covering at least the minimum topics listed in the rule.
items.quote: You must develop written operational policies and procedures that at a minimum address each of the following

items.requirement: The handbook must state the center's hours, days, and months of operation and its procedures for releasing children.
items.quote: (1) Hours, days, and months of operation [Medium]; (2) Procedures for the release of children [Medium]

items.requirement: The handbook must state illness and exclusion criteria and medication procedures or that medication is not dispensed.
items.quote: (3) Illness and exclusion criteria [Medium]; (4) Procedures for dispensing medication or a statement that medication is not dispensed [Medium]

items.requirement: The handbook must state procedures for handling medical emergencies and for parental notifications.
items.quote: (5) Procedures for handling medical emergencies [Medium]; (6) Procedures for parental notifications [Medium]

items.requirement: The handbook must include discipline and guidance consistent with Subchapter L.
items.quote: Discipline and guidance that is consistent with Subchapter L of this title (relating to Discipline and Guidance)

items.requirement: The handbook must include a safe sleep policy for infants from birth through 12 months old.
items.quote: Safe sleep policy for infants from birth through 12 months old

items.requirement: The handbook must state hearing and vision screening requirements and enrollment procedures, including how and when parents are notified of policy changes.
items.quote: (12) Hearing and vision screening requirements [Medium]; (13) Enrollment procedures, including how and when parents will be notified of policy changes

items.requirement: If applicable, the handbook must state transportation and water activity procedures.
items.quote: (14) Transportation, if applicable [Medium]; (15) Water activities, if applicable [Medium]

items.requirement: If applicable, the handbook must state field trip and animal procedures.
items.quote: (16) Field trips, if applicable [Medium]; (17) Animals, if applicable [Medium]

items.requirement: The handbook must promote indoor and outdoor physical activity consistent with Subchapter F.
items.quote: Promotion of indoor and outdoor physical activity that is consistent with Subchapter F of this chapter

items.requirement: If applicable, the handbook must state procedures for providing and applying insect repellant and sunscreen.
items.quote: Procedures for providing and applying, as needed, insect repellant and sunscreen, including what types will be used, if applicable [Medium]

items.requirement: The handbook must state parent rights consistent with Division 5 of Subchapter B.
items.quote: Parent rights that are consistent with the rules in Division 5 of this subchapter (relating to Parent Rights) [Medium]

items.requirement: The handbook must state procedures for parents to review and discuss questions or concerns with the director.
items.quote: Procedures for parents to review and discuss with the child-care center director any questions or concerns about the policies and procedures of the child-care center [Medium]

items.requirement: Children's records must be immediately accessible to caregivers during hours of operation for emergency use.
items.quote: All children’s records must be immediately accessible to caregivers during hours of operation for use in an emergency.

items.requirement: Employees must report suspected abuse, neglect, and exploitation to DFPS as required by law.
items.quote: Report suspected abuse, neglect, and exploitation to DFPS as specified in the Texas Family Code, §261.101.

items.requirement: Classroom ratios are based on the specified age of the children in the group and must not be exceeded.
items.quote: The classroom ratio is the number of children one caregiver may supervise and is shown in the following chart.

items.requirement: Infants must be placed face-up for sleep in their own crib unless a health-care professional documents a different position is medically necessary.
items.quote: You must place an infant in a face-up sleeping position in the infant's own crib, unless you have a completed Sleep Exception Form that includes a signed statement from a health-care professional stating that a different sleeping position for the child is medically necessary

items.requirement: There must be no harsh, cruel, or unusual treatment of any child, including prohibited discipline practices.
items.quote: There must be no harsh, cruel, or unusual treatment of any child.

items.requirement: Parents must be notified at least 48 hours in advance of a field trip with destination and expected return time.
items.quote: You must notify the parent of each child who will be on the field trip, indicating when and where the child will be going, and when the child is expected to return to the child-care center.

items.requirement: Meals and snacks must follow USDA CACFP meal patterns regardless of reimbursement participation.
items.quote: The meals and snacks must follow the meal patterns established by the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) Child and Adult Care Food Program (CACFP)

items.requirement: Unless licensed for get-well care, an ill child must not attend if the listed illness conditions exist.
items.quote: Unless you are licensed to provide get-well care, you must not allow an ill child to attend your child-care center if one or more of the following exists:

items.requirement: Medication may be administered only with parent authorization obtained in writing, electronically, or by telephone for a single dose.
items.quote: Authorization to administer medication to a child in your care must be obtained from the child’s parent:

items.requirement: A food allergy emergency plan is required for each child with a health-care-professional-diagnosed food allergy.
items.quote: You must have a food allergy emergency plan for each child with a known food allergy that has been diagnosed by a health-care professional.

items.requirement: A child may be released only to a parent or a person designated by the parent.
items.quote: You must release a child only to a parent or a person designated by the parent.

items.requirement: The center must practice a fire drill every month and children must be able to exit safely within three minutes.
items.quote: You must practice a fire drill every month. The children must be able to safely exit the building within three minutes
